title: Tutor teaching-behavior test: stuck / hint / close-enough / partial / wrong / correct
description: Tests the tutor's GENERIC teaching behavior (independent of subject matter) on the unit-1 question 'print("one") then print("two") — how many lines and what is on each?'. Seven scripted learner turns cover: stuck, asking to be told, a close-enough answer, a partial answer, a wrong answer, asking for a hint, and a fully correct answer. Structural behaviors (question count, hint-vs-full-answer, gave-an-explanation, stays-on-unit) are scored deterministically; fuzzy behaviors (accepted close enough, gentle correction, confirmed understanding, not too strict on wording) are checked by the optional LLM judge via the run-tutor-behavior-eval runner.

turns.learnerMessage: I think they show up on separate lines.
They print on the same line, like onetwo.
Two lines — 'one' on the first line and 'two' on the second, because each print() ends with a new line.
